newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-West Australia premier announces cabinet.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-West Australia premier announces cabinet.

text.p: Western Australian Premier Richard Court today announced his second term cabinet.

Three ministers have been dumped, four new ones have been appointed, a former minister who resigned in 1993 has returned to the ministry and the total number of ministers has been increased by one to 17.
Court said he was confident the new 'mix' would be able to oversee the delivery of social and economic dividends to the people of Western Australia as the State moved into the 21st century.
"It makes the most of existing ministerial experience and a talented group of members who have already proven their ability when given specific projects as backbenchers," Court said.
The re-shuffle followed the Coalition's success in the pre-Christmas election. Court also had to fill a vacancy left by the retirement of Planning and Heritage Minister, Richard Lewis.
The National Party lost one of its four ministers - Ron Weise - because of the increase in the number of Liberal MPs in the new Parliament.
The other two Ministers dumped were Roger Nicholls (Water Resources) and Kevin Minson (Disability Services).
* Hills MLA Mike Day who gets the Police and Emergency Services portfolio;
* Yokine MLA Dr Kim Hames (Aboriginal Affairs, Water Resources and Housing);
* Alfred Cove MLA Mike Shave (Lands, Fair Trading and Parliamentary and Electoral Affairs);
* Ballajura MLA Rhonda Parker (Family and Children's Services, Seniors and Women's Interests); and
* Murdoch MLA Mike Board (Youth, Works and Services and Muticultural and Ethnic Affairs).
Court said the new Cabinet also reflected changes which would allow a number of Ministers to better focus on particular portfolios.
However some ministers retained all their previous portfolio responsibilities.

They were: Deputy Premier Hendy Cowan (Commerce and Trade, Regional Development and Small Business); Colin Barnett (Education, Resources Development, Energy); Monty House (Primary Industry and Fisheries); Max Evans (Finance, Racing and Gaming) and Eric Charlton (Transport).
The new cabinet was sworn in today at Government House.
